title: PR #16 — Login and secure note item editors
description: Build the create/edit surfaces for login items and secure notes, encrypting on save and integrating with the optimistic cache and outbox. Requirement IDs: TASK-40, TASK-41.
acceptanceCriteria: Login editor supports name, username, password, multiple URLs, notes, folder, favorite, TOTP secret, and custom fields with a hidden toggle
Secure note editor supports name, multiline body, folder, and favorite
Saving encrypts with the in-memory vault key and writes through the outbox; the server stores ciphertext only
A query against D1 after a save shows no plaintext name, username, password, or note body
Required name validation blocks save with an inline error
Unsaved changes trigger a confirm dialog on navigation, route change, and browser close
Delete from the editor moves the item to trash
A 50KB note body saves and reloads correctly; a larger body is blocked client-side with a clear message
Create, edit, and delete round-trip correctly after a reload

steps.details: Create `app/features/vault-item/vault-item.schema.ts` with Zod schemas for the decrypted plaintext of `login` and `note`, including limits (name 256 chars, username 256, password 1024, 10 URLs, 20 custom fields, note body 50KB). Reuse the same schema before encryption so client and future clients agree.

Create `app/routes/vault.$itemId.tsx` as a transport-only route plus the page entry `app/features/vault-item/vault-item.tsx` with `index.ts`, `components/`, and `vault-item.hooks.ts`. Handle both `new` and existing ids, with a shared header (title, favorite toggle, delete, save) and a form container. Use the same route for create with `id = 'new'`.

Add fields with proper `autocomplete="off"`, `spellcheck="false"`, and `type="password"` for secrets. Include a reveal toggle, a generate button wired to the TASK-16 generator (stub the callback if not merged), a custom-fields repeater with hidden flags, and a TOTP secret field with format validation.
Add a name field and a textarea with a character counter and a 50KB hard limit. Keep it minimal: no rich text, no Markdown rendering.

steps.description: Wire save through encryption and outbox
steps.details: On save: validate → build plaintext object → `sealItem` → enqueue create or update with the current `rev` → update the cache → navigate back to the list with a saved indicator. On 409, show a conflict dialog offering reload or save-as-copy; do not silently overwrite.
Track a dirty flag from react-hook-form. Register a `beforeunload` handler while dirty and intercept in-app navigation with a confirm dialog. Reset the flag after a successful save.
Add a delete action that soft-deletes through the outbox, updates the cache, and returns to the list. Show a toast with an undo affordance that restores within the toast lifetime.

Playwright: create a login item with a known password, then query local D1 via a test helper and assert the plaintext does not appear in `data_ct`. Repeat for a note body. Also assert reload shows the decrypted values.

technicalNotes: Never put secret values into URLs, analytics, or error reports.
Do not render secret field values in SSR output; editors are client-rendered after unlock.
Use client-generated item ids so offline creates and retries stay idempotent.
Custom fields are part of the encrypted payload, not separate columns.
The item plaintext schema is a shared contract for future extension and Android clients.
